thread:
ashley: kicking off ORD-edge perf validation run — bootstrap + kernel/driver checks + baseline. putting checklist here for handoff to oncall/eng. pls chime if i've missed anything. :clipboard:
ben: thx. main goals: p95 latency under 12ms for small chat model, stable throughput >= 220 tokens/s per GPU under steady-state, no >2% error rate on model startup paths.
cheng: note: ORD nodes are A100S with 80GB NVLink. verify driver + nvidia-container-runtime + device-plugin alignment. we hit a weird cudnn mismatch last time.
oliver: quick command snippets i used in SEA that you can copy:
```
# check driver/kernel modules
nvidia-smi -q | head -n 30
modinfo nvidia | grep -i version
uname -a
# runtimes
docker info | grep -i runtime
kubectl get pods -n gpu-system -o wide
```
paige: add NCCL health and NVLink checks to the list. run nccl-tests/all_reduce for 10 minutes with socket affinity.
ashley: good call. adding to checklist: 1) kernel version & DKMS modules, 2) nvidia-driver verified, 3) nvidia-container-runtime + docker shim, 4) kube device plugin ready, 5) MIG config (if applicable), 6) NCCL ring health, 7) perf smoke: p50/p95/p99, 8) stress soak 30m, 9) cost/throughput calc, 10) handoff note.
sre-bot: [deploy-bot] ORD-edge cluster bootstrap completed by @ashley at 1938455900. status: 72 nodes registered, 68 ready, 4 provisioning.
ben: logs: one node failed DKMS build — kernel-5.10.152 mismatch. ashley can you repro with the install script?
ashley: repro step: ran our bootstrap on the failed node, saw build error in /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/550.104/build/make.log -> missing header for 5.10.152. workaround: install linux-headers-5.10.152 then re-run dkms. patching installer to include headers check.
cheng: after patch, full fleet now shows device-plugin ready: kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable | grep gpu
oliver: perf smoke results (single-worker job across 4 GPUs): p50=3.4ms, p95=10.8ms, p99=22.9ms, throughput=240 tokens/s (steady). attached snippet from the run:
```
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z INFO run: batch_size=8, seq=512
2026-03-18T14:12:33Z METRIC p50=3.4ms p95=10.8ms p99=22.9ms qps=240
2026-03-18T14:42:33Z METRIC p50=3.6ms p95=11.1ms p99=24.0ms qps=238 (soak)
```
paige: NCCL tests stable, all_reduce latency baseline looks fine. no NVLink drops in dmesg.
ben: cost note: ORD reserved rack price is +9% vs SFO; at 240 tokens/s per GPU we estimate $0.012/token-hour (back-of-envelope) when factoring utilization assumptions. ops_lead: flag — we should include a brief note in handoff about cost delta and recommended burst/capacity tiers to avoid surprises for customers migrating.
sre-bot: [perf-checker] p95 threshold check passed (<=12ms) for job 1938456000-ord-smoke.
ashley: open items: 1) add linux-headers install to bootstrap script (in PR), 2) add driver version check to console onboarding, 3) update runbook note for oncall to run nccl-tests after any kernel patch. tagging @ops_lead for handoff.
ops_lead: ack — i'll pick up the handoff doc. pls paste the one-pager snippet i can drop into the customer console and oncall runbook.
ashley: one-pager for handoff (short):
- cluster: ord-edge (ord-az1..az3)
- node type: A100S-80GB, kernel: 5.10.152 (ensure headers), driver: 550.104, cudnn: 8.6.x
- perf baselines: p50=~3.5ms, p95=~11ms, throughput=~240 tokens/s per GPU (seq512, bs8)
- known issues: dkms failure if linux-headers missing; nvlink flakiness under heavy NCCL if kernel mismatch present
- handoff checklist: run `nvidia-smi -q`, `kubectl -n gpu-system get pods`, run `./perf/smoke.sh --seq 512 --bs 8 --duration 600`, then `./nccl-tests/all_reduce -t 600`
ops_lead: looks good. i'll add cost note and escalate checklist to longhand. also set an SLA ticket template for Dedicated migrations.
ben: small ask: can we add a quick telemetry flag in the bootstrap that ships kernel/driver versions to console for first-boot? would speed up debug.
ashley: yeah, adding that to PR. patch reference: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/ord-bootstrap/pull/57
cheng: post-handoff: schedule 24h soak with periodic perf samples and an automated regression alert if p95 climbs >1.5x baseline. also store sample traces to s3 for triage.
oliver: i'll run the soak job tonight and leave notes in the runbook channel. if anything spikes i'll ping here. :eyes:
paige: thanks everyone — great teamwork. closing thread once ops_lead confirms handoff doc is in place. :thumbsup:
